hypothesis: Who the household is (demographics) and when the snapshot is (calendar) predict 4-week spend.
transformation_description: Baseline: demographic codes, has_demographics, snapshot day index, week-of-year.

hypothesis: A household's recent purchase history (spend in trailing 7/28/56/84/168d windows, trip counts, basket size, recency, product/store counts) predicts its next-4-week spend far better than demographics.
transformation_description: Added ~30 transaction-history features over multiple trailing windows; trained XGBoost on train snapshots only.
reasoning_summary: Past spend is the strongest known predictor of future spend; multi-window history captures level, trend and cadence that demographics cannot.

hypothesis: Marketing exposure (campaign targeting counts/recency by type, coupon redemptions) and household demographics (ordinal-encoded age, income level, size, homeowner, kids) add signal beyond transaction history for predicting 4-week future spend.
transformation_description: Added ~19 features over E001: campaign targeting counts/recency (ever/28d/active, per TypeA/B/C), coupon redemption counts/recency, and 8 ordinal demographic encodings; same XGBoost setup.
reasoning_summary: Campaigns and coupons directly incentivize purchases in the next weeks, and demographics capture household capacity to spend; both should reduce error beyond pure purchase-history features.

hypothesis: The target's error is heavy-tailed (median spend 73.5, mean 136.9), so training XGBoost on absolute error instead of squared error yields better validation MAE.
transformation_description: Same ~30 transaction-history features as E001; changed only the XGBoost objective from reg:squarederror to reg:absoluteerror (1500 trees, lr=0.03, depth 6, subsample/colsample 0.8, min_child_weight 5).
reasoning_summary: MAE is the metric and the spend distribution is heavy-tailed, so an L1 objective optimizes the conditional median, which should reduce validation MAE relative to the L2-trained E001 model.

hypothesis: Future 4-week spend is best predicted by an exponentially-weighted blend of past 4-week-window spends (cycle-aligned lags), because grocery spending is autocorrelated at the 4-week cycle; adding richer basket-structure, discount, and diversity features on top of E001 plus an MAE (reg:absoluteerror) objective reduces heavy-tail error.
transformation_description: Rebuilt features: cycle-aligned 4w-window lags (lag1-3) with an exp4w_blend = 0.5*lag0+0.3*lag1+0.2*lag2 headline feature, weekly spend profile stats, basket/gap structure, discount shares, dept diversity, demographics; XGBoost reg:absoluteerror, lr 0.05, depth 6, early-stopped on snapshot 431.
reasoning_summary: E003 showed MAE objective helps; the top feature importance of exp4w_blend (0.54) suggests the model leans on a hand-crafted weighted blend of past 4w windows — making that blend richer and the objective match the metric should cut MAE below 63.1.

hypothesis: The 4-week-ahead spend distribution is right-skewed, so the conditional-median objective (reg:quantileerror, alpha=0.5) is a better match to MAE than pseudo-Huber, improving on E004's huber head.
transformation_description: Same feats_v3 features as E004; changed only the XGBoost objective from reg:pseudohubererror to reg:quantileerror with quantile_alpha=0.5 (n_estimators=1200, lr=0.03, depth=7, trained on all 13 train snapshots).
reasoning_summary: MAE is minimized by the conditional median, and the quantile objective directly targets it; pseudo-Huber only approximates it. ES-snapshot checks showed q50 MAE 61.9 vs huber 62.4.

hypothesis: The 4-week-ahead spend is highly persistent: blending the model's conditional-median prediction with the household's own exponentially-weighted trailing 4w-window spend (0.7*model + 0.3*exp4w_blend), and using shallower trees (depth 4, min_child_weight 20), reduces MAE versus E005 (depth 6, no blend).
transformation_description: Same feats_v3 features; XGBoost quantile(0.5) with max_depth 4, min_child_weight 20; final prediction = 0.7*model + 0.3*exp4w_blend.
reasoning_summary: Local held-out snapshots (403/431) showed the blend cuts MAE ~0.6-0.8 and shallow trees another ~0.3; residual correlations of new candidate features were near zero, so no feature change was made.

hypothesis: Purchase-mix structure (commodity concentration, repeat-purchase loyalty, private-brand share, stock-up behaviour, store loyalty) signals household consumption style and improves 4-week-ahead spend prediction beyond raw spend history.
transformation_description: Added 12 product-mix/loyalty/stock-up features over trailing 84d (hhi_84, n_commodities_84, top_comm_share_84, repeat_rate_84, private_share_84, grocery_share_84, stockup_max_84, store_loyalty_84, wkend_share_84, cycle-aligned lag1-3 spends) on top of the v3 set; removed the exp4w_blend shrinkage (clean CV showed pure model >= blended). XGBoost reg:quantileerror q=0.5, depth 4, mcw 20.

hypothesis: Future 4-week spend is best predicted as the persistence blend (exp4w_blend) plus a learned *correction*: training XGBoost to predict the residual y − exp4w_blend (rather than y directly) and adding it back lets the model focus on deviations from persistence, reducing MAE.

hypothesis: The conditional-median model is slightly under-dispersed for MAE: nudging the quantile above 0.5, adding spend×tenure/trips interaction features, and averaging two differently-biased learners (XGBoost quantile + histogram-GBM with absolute-error loss) reduces variance and tail shrinkage of the prediction.

reasoning_summary: Internal out-of-time CV (train ≤375, eval 403/431) showed each component alone or in combination lowers MAE vs the E011 recipe (62.32 → 62.11), so the combined variant should beat E011's 61.836 on validation.

hypothesis: Averaging a diverse-hyperparameter XGBoost quantile(0.5) ensemble trained on the raw target with one trained on the residual (future_spend_4w minus the exp4w_blend persistence forecast) reduces variance and captures persistence beyond the hand-crafted blend, lowering validation MAE below E011's 61.836.
transformation_description: Same feats_v4 features; replaced the single-model XGBoost with an 8-config diverse bag (max_depth 4-6, min_child_weight 20-80, seeds 2-10), each trained twice (raw target and residual target), final prediction = 0.6*plain_bag + 0.4*(exp4w_blend + residual_bag).

hypothesis: Training the quantile-median bag on all 13 train snapshots (including day 431, closest to validation) plus seed diversity reduces validation MAE relative to E013, which excluded day 431 from training.
